name: 2019 livery
description: White, with the rear fuselage teal behind a straight diagonal lime-green line that runs from the belly ahead of the tail up to the fin; a big light green shamrock on the teal fin; teal engines; 'Aer Lingus' in teal with a small green shamrock above the forward windows.

sources.title: Aer Lingus Airbus A321neo EI-LRH IAD VA2 (CC BY-SA 4.0)
sources.note: Left side, side-on, 2025-04-30: the diagonal, title, shamrocks, engines.

sources.title: Airbus A321neo EI-LRH MD2 (CC BY-SA 4.0)
sources.note: Right side from below, 2025-07-26: belly white forward, teal aft; the same on the right.

sources.title: Aer Lingus Airbus A321neo EI-LRH IAD VA1 (CC BY-SA 4.0)

logos.description: The Aer Lingus shamrock, simplified in 2019: three heart-shaped leaves round a point with a short curved stem, flat light green, large on the teal fin.
The shamrock again, small, just after the 'Aer Lingus' title.
A small Irish tricolor just after the registration, under the rear windows.

titles.style: The 2019 Aer Lingus wordmark: a clean medium-weight geometric sans, capital A and L, above the forward windows behind door 1.

notes: Measured on A321neo EI-LRH (left side side-on, right side from below). The diagonal is a straight line in side view. The aircraft names under the forward windows and the reg on the fin tip are not drawn. A330s and A320s share the scheme; some A320ceos may still wear the 1990s scheme (white over green belly, 'aer lingus' in green, green fin with the white shamrock) until repainted. Re-checked 2026-11-15 on EI-LRH (left side, near side-on, 2025-04-30): the title runs x 0.143-0.262, its baseline about 0.25 m over the window tops and its capitals about 0.5 m tall (it had sat higher, y 0.47); lowercase 0.63 of the capitals; the straight diagonal reduced to its ends.
history: Replaced Skyarium v1's approximation (2026-11). The 2019 scheme replaced the green-belly livery with the white shamrock on a green tail.
